mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05) when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.6%, it indicates accelerating inflation, which compresses the real discount rate and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior low-inflation periods (t-test p > 0.05) when trigger is satisfied.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE (≥ 0.2 percentage points) signals a labor-market softening without wage inflation, which tends to lower equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 5% in a month AND UNRATE falls by ≥ 0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable labor-market tightening episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in HOUST above 2% for three consecutive months indicates strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during prior periods of similar HOUST growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO exceeding 8% while FEDFUNDS remains below 1% signals a supply-side shock (e.g., manufacturing contraction), which tends to reduce market optimism and drive negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 8% in a month AND FEDFUNDS < 1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not deviate significantly from a baseline of normal supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS rises by more than 10% in a month, it suggests excess liquidity in the repo market, which lowers real rates and is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of normal liquidity (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in UNRATE below 3% for four consecutive months in a non-recessionary economy is interpreted as a wage-stagnation regime that tends to depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable wage-growth regimes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both GDPC1 (demand) and PAYEMS (employment) for two consecutive months predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return, as it signals dual momentum in consumption and labor markets.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by ≥ 3% AND PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during periods of single-momentum demand (t-test p > 0.05).
